question: Should OpenClaw accept the ongoing owner-lifecycle obligation required by a native prepared-statement cache in the shared and per-agent state database owners?
rationale: The implementation intentionally trades repeated prepare work for retained native statement objects, and correctness depends on a cross-cutting disposal invariant rather than a local query-helper contract alone.

options.title: Accept with owner sign-off
options.body: Rebase the PR, require green checks, and merge once the state-database owner confirms the audited clear-before-close paths cover the supported handle lifecycle.

options.title: Keep execution stateless
options.body: Decline the cache and retain per-call statement preparation to avoid a persistent native-resource lifecycle obligation.

recommendation.title: Accept with owner sign-off
recommendation.body: Rebase the PR, require green checks, and merge once the state-database owner confirms the audited clear-before-close paths cover the supported handle lifecycle.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant ownership is the shared-state and agent-state database area, but individual attribution could not be established without the required git-history commands.
